title: Universality of Energy-Space Entanglement in Quantum Impurity Models
abstract: Entanglement entropy (EE) is commonly studied using real-space bipartitions. We show that, in quantum impurity models, an energy-space bipartition, equivalent to the momentum-space bipartition of the bath, can display universal behavior. Motivated by poor man's scaling, we logarithmically discretize the bath and partition it into high- and low-energy sectors. For models with Fermi-liquid fixed points, including the Anderson model and fully screened or underscreened Kondo models, the low-energy EE flows to constants independent of model parameters. These constants are integer multiples of $\ln 2$ plus corrections that depend only on the logarithmic discretization parameter $Λ$. We show that scale invariance of the fixed-point wavefunction in energy space maps to effective translation invariance along a one-dimensional chain, allowing the fixed points to be classified by one-dimensional topological band theory. With low-energy chiral symmetry, each $\ln 2$ contribution originates from a topological edge mode. We also study transitions between distinct Fermi-liquid fixed points using the local-singlet--Kondo-singlet transition in a two-orbital Anderson model driven by an inter-orbital antiferromagnetic coupling. The local-singlet phase has an effectively decoupled impurity and nearly vanishing EE, whereas the Kondo-singlet phase has finite EE larger than $\ln 2$ per spin and orbital. When chiral symmetry holds at low energies, this distinction corresponds to a topological transition of the effective bath chain. At the non-Fermi-liquid critical point, the EE develops an unstable plateau. Its $Λ$ dependence resembles that of the overscreened two-channel Kondo model, supporting universality within the same non-Fermi-liquid universality class.
summary: This work develops a novel method using energy-space bipartitioning to calculate entanglement entropy in quantum impurity models. It demonstrates that this EE exhibits universal, parameter-independent plateaus at Fermi-liquid fixed points, linking these values to topological invariants derived from the bath structure. The findings provide powerful diagnostic tools for distinguishing between different correlated ground states and characterizing quantum phase transitions.
main_problem: The study investigates universal behaviors of entanglement entropy (EE) by employing an energy-space bipartition in quantum impurity models, moving beyond standard real or momentum space cuts.
main_result: For Fermi-liquid fixed points, the low-energy EE flows to parameter-independent constants related to topological edge modes; furthermore, the EE distinguishes between different correlated phases like local-singlet and Kondo-singlet states.
method: The analysis uses logarithmic discretization of the bath energy (poor man's scaling) and calculates entanglement entropy using DMRG on an effective Hamiltonian representation (star/MPO).
model_or_system: The focus is on quantum impurity models, including the Anderson model and various Kondo models, coupled to a fermionic bath. The formalism utilizes MPO representations for numerical stability.
key_observables: Energy-space Entanglement Entropy ($S_{\Lambda}(E)$) and its low-energy plateau value $S_{\Lambda}(0)$.
important_parameters: Kondo temperature ($T_K$), logarithmic discretization parameter ($\Lambda$), interaction couplings ($U, J_K$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the low-energy physics is governed by universal fixed points and relies on mapping the system to an effective 1D chain structure.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate $S_{\Lambda}(E)$ for various models (Anderson, Kondo) showing saturation plateaus; one figure compares EE across ten Altland-Zirnbauer symmetry classes based on spectral hybridization.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the energy-space bipartition method, applying it to Fermi-liquid fixed points to show universality and topological classification (Chiral Symmetry), examining quantum phase transitions between different correlated states, and finally generalizing the findings across various Altland-Zirnbauer symmetry classes.
why_interesting: The use of entanglement entropy as a diagnostic tool for classifying quantum critical points and determining universal properties in strongly interacting impurity systems is highly relevant to understanding open quantum systems dynamics.
